builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
summary: The method replaces per-prediction trust in foundation-model perturbation response outputs with a calibrated confidence score, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, motivated by the finding that the ST decoder's first attention layer is low-rank (projecting onto 4-32 fixed directions preserves mean PDC). It requires storing training response vectors and computing nearest-neighbor cosine distances per prediction, plus calibration data to set thresholds; the underlying model and decoder are unchanged, so no retraining or extra GPU capacity is needed. It can fail when predictions are reliable but far from all training responses (false low confidence), when the training set poorly covers the test distribution, and its validation is specific to the STATE ST decoder and CRISPRi/drug perturbation settings, so transfer to other architectures or assay types is unverified.
rationale: The score is cheap to compute on constrained infrastructure and directly supports experiment prioritization, but its reliability guarantees are demonstrated only for a specific decoder and perturbation domain, so workload-specific validation is required before production reliance.
technique: Per-prediction reliability score for perturbation response prediction

claims.statement: The method replaces per-prediction trust in foundation-model perturbation response outputs with a calibrated confidence score, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, motivated by the finding that the ST decoder's first attention layer is low-rank (projecting onto 4-32 fixed directions preserves mean PDC). It requires storing training response vectors and computing nearest-neighbor cosine distances per prediction, plus calibration data to set thresholds; the underlying model and decoder are unchanged, so no retraining or extra GPU capacity is needed. It can fail when predictions are reliable but far from all training responses (false low confidence), when the training set poorly covers the test distribution, and its validation is specific to the STATE ST decoder and CRISPRi/drug perturbation settings, so transfer to other architectures or assay types is unverified.

The predicted-NN-distance score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC), close to the 0.88 obtained using the observed response; thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across three encoders and four cell lines and remain predictive for drug perturbations.
